feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Trump staffing changes post-midterms signal he's battle ready
entry.summary: President Trump is making changes to his inner circle that signal how he may approach divided government.

entry.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
entry.summary: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.

entry.title: How will Democrats approach foreign policy after their midterm win?
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Thomas Wright, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, about his piece in Foreign Affairs titled The Fight for the Future of Democratic Foreign Policy.

entry.title: The world's largest telecoms firm is on trial and the outcome has global implications
entry.summary: Huawei, the world's biggest telecommunications company, is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions.

entry.title: This podcast explores explores why things made by hand are so special
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Sam Dingman, host of The Analogs podcast from NPR member station KJZZ.

entry.title: What makes Stephen King books work so well on the big screen?
entry.summary: Fifty years after the release of Carrie, the first Stephen King movie adaptation, two fans assess what the writer's cinematic legacy.

entry.title: Trying to find true owners, Paris' Musee D'Orsay exhibits art looted by Nazis
entry.summary: A new permanent exhibition at Paris' Musee d'Orsay showcases works of art suspected to have been looted by Nazis during the Second World War in France. Experts are trying to find the true owners or their descendants.

entry.title: Israeli president invites Netanyahu's opposition leader to broker new government
entry.summary: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.

entry.title: Texas's 'Blue Tsunami' has former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke 'over the moon'
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.

entry.title: The surprising and often forgotten history of economic populism in Texas
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Austin-based political commentator David Griscom. He authored a book titled The Myth of Red Texas which tells the story of economic populism in Texas.
